reviewedBoundaries: BLOCK context is awaited closed before editing browser Preferences and reopening the same private profile.
Preferences must be a regular non-symlink file smaller than 1MiB, protected by the exact OWNER marker and prior cookies=2 setting; recovery explicitly sets cookies=1.

Temporary profile is generated below canonical os.tmpdir with a fixed prefix; finally rechecks canonical parent, real path, non-symlink and OWNER before recursive deletion. Close failures remain fatal and do not claim profile cleanup.

Credential fallback observer returns only numeric counts. Supplied private values, URL fields, storage keys/values, page errors and user names are not returned. The private preauth challenge is removed before progress persistence.
Unexpected pageerror events preserve only fixed current stage and count; zero errors is required both before success and after pending observations at final cleanup.
Dialog initial activeElement containment is checked before keyboard cycling; recovery uses fresh employee primary login and verifies real SSO/console cookies in the same explicit ALLOW profile.
limitations: The cited Chromium results use an actual browser with a controlled HTTP fixture; this review did not rerun them.
The new SaaS HTTPS dialog/pageerror/fallback/recovery assertions still require the next owned source run; r4 actual9PASS is not rewritten.
PUBLIC no-secret management DOM and long consent subfacts are outside these three file changes.
